subject.title: [Feature]: Enrich before_tool_call event with action classification and input provenance

question: Should `before_tool_call` expose a host-owned action/provenance contract now, and should that contract be an enum, capability flags, Security Matrix facts, or deferred until the broader tool metadata design lands?
rationale: This is a public plugin SDK and security-boundary decision; automation can verify the missing fields, but it cannot choose what provenance plugins may see or which taxonomy OpenClaw should support long term.

options.title: Design the hook contract here
options.body: Keep this issue open as the focused design/implementation target for `before_tool_call` action facts and sanitized provenance after maintainer security review.

options.title: Make capability descriptors canonical first
options.body: Treat the tool descriptor issues as the first landing step, then return here to expose those facts through the hook.

options.title: Fold into Security Matrix
options.body: Let the Security Matrix runtime-fact model own the taxonomy and close this only after a merged implementation exposes equivalent hook facts.

recommendation.title: Design the hook contract here
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the focused design/implementation target for `before_tool_call` action facts and sanitized provenance after maintainer security review.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history shows `steipete` on the central hook/session/runtime paths, making him the best available routing owner for the SDK/security-boundary choice.
